s_open.name: 14:55, Wednesday
s_open.title: 14:55, Wednesday
s_open.body:
You are covering a shift for Danni, who called in sick.

Rachel, 24. She works Wednesdays at a garden centre on the north side of town. The roster says collect her at 3:00 and drive her to physio at 3:30.

You have never met her. You were sent an address and a time. You do not have her mobile number, and she does not have yours — the office does not give out workers' numbers.

You are in the car park, five minutes early. The only thing you have is last week's note.

s_note.name: The note
s_note.title: Last Wednesday's note
s_note.body:
Took Rachel to work. All good. She seemed a little tired in the car.

That is the whole note. Eleven words.

q_arrive.name: She is not out front
q_arrive.title: Rachel is not at the front entrance
q_arrive.body:
It is 2:55. The roster says front entrance. Two staff are having a smoke by the door and there is no sign of Rachel.

Physio is a twelve minute drive.

What do you do?

choices.label: Wait in the car — she'll come out

s_ring.name: You ring Rachel
s_ring.title: You ring Rachel
s_ring.body:
You do not have her number. You ring the office to ask for it, and they will not give it out over the phone — which is the correct answer, and you would want the same rule applied to your own number.

They offer to try her themselves. They ring. It goes to voicemail.

Rachel does not pick up numbers she does not recognise. She has never met you.

It is 3:03. You are still in the car park and you still do not know where she is.

s_wait.name: You wait
s_wait.title: You wait in the car
s_wait.body:
You wait. At 3:05 you get out and walk to the front doors.

Rachel has been sitting on a pallet by the loading door at the back since two o'clock. She always waits there — the front is loud and there is nowhere to sit.

She rang the office at ten past two and got voicemail. She did not try again. The text she had said three o'clock, so she assumed her lift was running late.

You leave at 3:20. Physio gives a fifteen minute grace period. You do not make it.

s_inside.name: You go inside
s_inside.title: You go inside and ask
s_inside.body:
A supervisor points you round the back without looking up. "She'll be on the pallet by the loading door. She's always there."

Rachel finished at two. She does some Wednesdays, depending on the deliveries.

"Danni usually gets here about then," he says, and goes back to what he was doing.

You make physio with three minutes to spare.

s_office.name: You ring the office
s_office.title: You ring the office
s_office.body:
Someone answers and opens the file while you wait. The note says what you have already read.

They ring the garden centre, then ring you back at 3:09. Rachel waits at the loading door. She finished at two today.

"That's odd," they say. "The roster's always had her at three."

You make physio, just.

q_note.name: Your turn to write
q_note.title: You are writing your own note now
q_note.body:
Next Wednesday somebody covers Rachel. It might be Danni. It might be someone who has never met her.

Which of these would you write?

choices.label: "Collected Rachel from work and drove her to physio. All went well."
choices.feedback: "All went well" is your judgement, and the next worker cannot act on it. They still will not know where she waits, or that she sometimes finishes at two.

choices.label: "Rachel waits on the pallet by the loading door at the back, not the front entrance. Some Wednesdays she finishes at 2:00 instead of 3:00. Collected her at 3:05 and drove her to physio."
choices.feedback: This is the one. Where she waits, when she finishes, what you did. The next worker drives straight round the back, and Rachel does not sit on a pallet for an hour.

choices.label: "Rachel was annoyed about being kept waiting again."
choices.feedback: "Annoyed" is what you concluded, not what you saw — and it puts the problem on Rachel rather than on the missing information. The next worker now meets an annoyed woman before they meet Rachel.

s_end.name: Debrief
s_end.title: Three things failed. None of them is a person.
s_end.body:
Rachel finished at 2:00. The roster said 3:00.

Danni knew that. On the Wednesdays Rachel finishes early, Danni just turns up early — she has done for months. From where Danni stood there was never a problem to report. She was handling it.

So the roster still says 3:00, because nobody ever needed it to say anything else.

Then Danni got sick.

The roster does not show that Rachel finishes at 2:00 some weeks. Not yours to fix — but worth telling the office, and section 5 is where you do that.

The phone went to voicemail when Rachel rang at ten past two. Also not yours.

And Danni's memory was doing a job the system thought it was doing itself. The day she was away, the system fell back on what it actually knew — the roster — and the roster was wrong.

Writing it down would not have got Rachel to physio on time. It would have sent you round the back at 2:56 instead of standing at the front until 3:05. And it would have told whoever sets the roster that three o'clock is wrong.

Drove Rachel to the garden centre for her 9:00 start. She waits at the loading door round the back when she finishes, not the front — the front is loud and there is nowhere to sit. Some Wednesdays she finishes at 2:00 instead of 3:00, depending on deliveries. Collected her at 3:05 and drove her to physio.

About a minute longer to write.

A note is not for you. It is for the day you are not there.
